Hi Helen — great to connect on Friday. Wanted to send a short recap and next steps so we don’t lose momentum.

Recap from the call:
- Use case: fraud alert enrichment for transaction stream (low-latency, 80ms p95 target).
- Pilot scope: 10k transactions/day, run in Redwood Dedicated for first 90 days.
- Data: tokenized transaction metadata only; customer confirmed no raw PII in payload.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I shared the proposed SOW + contract with counsel (attachment: redlines_FTC_v1.pdf). Can you confirm who on your legal/procurement side will own review?
2) Procurement asked for an MSA redline summary — we can provide a short table of material changes.
3) Can you share target procurement timing? Is finance alignment already in flight?

If helpful I can loop in our contracts manager (Marissa) or our privacy lead. I’ve attached the redlines we sent to counsel and a draft mutual action plan.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 15-min call to unblock if that helps.

—Sean

Sean — forwarding in case you want me to engage directly with Helen’s counsel. From the redlines I reviewed there are three items that typically slow procurement: indemnity language, data residency clause, and termination for convenience. I suggest a 15-min sync (internal) to align on fallback suggestions we can propose to move this along:

- Option A: Provide a limited indemnity with dollar cap tied to pilot value.
- Option B: Offer an EEA-only data residency addendum as a concession if they require it.
- Option C: Shorten mutual termination notice to 60 days for the pilot (instead of 90).

I can draft a 1-page redline summary for procurement and send it to Helen’s counsel — will copy you and Monica. Want me to proceed?

—Marissa
